walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: denary to hexadecimal

steps.text: A similar question. Convert the denary number 180 to hexadecimal.
Divide by 16: 180 ÷ 16 = 11 remainder 4. 11 sixteens, 4 left over.
The whole number, 11, is the left digit. 11 is one digit: B. The remainder 4 is the right digit.
A bigger number: 330 ÷ 16 = 20 remainder 10. 20 is more than 15, so divide 20 by 16 again: 1 remainder 4.
Read the digits: 1, then 4, then the first remainder 10 = A. So 330 is 14A. Check: 256 + 64 + 10 = 330.
Now do the same for the question: divide by 16, keep each remainder, and change 10 to 15 into A to F.
steps.visual: divide → remainder → A to F → check

steps.label: Why Hexadecimal Is Used
steps.content:
1.1 Number Systems

Why Hexadecimal Is Used

Year 11

  • Today: why people write binary as hexadecimal.
  • Where hexadecimal is used: MAC addresses, colour codes, error codes and more.
  • How to write the reasons so they earn the marks.
Think → Pair → ShareIf the computer works in binary, why would anyone write numbers in another system?Show the answer

People find long binary numbers hard to read, so they write them in a shorter way.

steps.label: The Computer Only Stores Binary
steps.content:
The Computer Only Stores Binary

Think → Pair → ShareA computer stores the colour #2F15D6. Predict: what is really inside the computer, and who is the hexadecimal for?Show the worked answer

Inside the computer it is only binary: 24 bits. The hexadecimal #2F15D6 is how it is shown to a person.

  • The computer always stores and processes binary.
  • Hexadecimal is how binary is shown to people.
  • One digit = 4 bits, so hexadecimal is 4 times shorter.
  • It does not save memory, make files smaller or make the computer faster.
What the computer stores (24 bits)
0010 1111 0001 0101 1101 0110
What a person reads (6 digits)
2F15D6

steps.label: Predict: Does Hexadecimal Save Memory?
steps.content:
Predict: Does Hexadecimal Save Memory?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can a different way of writing a number not change how much memory it uses?Show the answer

The computer stores the bits, not the way we write them. The same bits use the same memory.

items.prompt: A memory address is shown as A2F instead of 101000101111. How much memory does the address take up inside the computer?
options: Less, because A2F has fewer digits
The same: it is still stored as 12 bits
More, because letters take more space
items.explain: The computer stores the same 12 bits either way. A2F is only a shorter way to show them to a person.

items.prompt: Which statement about hexadecimal is true?
options: The CPU processes hexadecimal faster than binary
Hexadecimal is easier for people to read than binary
items.explain: The computer only uses binary, so hexadecimal cannot change speed or file size. It helps the person reading the number.

steps.label: Compare: Which Is Easier to Copy?
steps.content:
Compare: Which Is Easier to Copy?

Think → Pair → ShareAna copies a value in binary. Sam copies the same value in hexadecimal. Each makes one slip. Predict: whose slip is easier to spot, and why?Show the worked answer

Sam's. His value is only 4 digits, so one wrong digit stands out. Ana's is 16 bits of 1s and 0s that all look alike.

  • Fewer digits = quicker to read, write and type.
  • Fewer digits = less chance of a mistake.
  • A mistake is easier to spot, so debugging is easier.
  • It takes up less space on the screen.
Ana (binary)
Value:
0011 1100 0100 1101
Ana wrote:
0011 1100 0000 1101
Can you see the slip?
Sam (hexadecimal)
Value:
3C4D
Sam wrote:
3C4B
The last digit is wrong.

steps.content:
Exam Question: Which Statement Is Incorrect?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is hexadecimal called base 16?Show the answer

It has 16 digits, 0 to 9 and A to F, and each column is worth 16 times the one to its right.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2024, Question 2(a). Hypertext markup language (HTML) colour codes can be represented as hexadecimal. Tick one box to show which statement about the hexadecimal number system is incorrect.

items.prompt: Which statement about the hexadecimal number system is incorrect?
options: It uses the values 0 to 9 and A to F.
It can be used as a shorter representation of binary.
It can be used to represent error codes.
items.explain: Hexadecimal is base 16. Denary is the base 10 system.

items.prompt: Give two benefits, to users, of converting binary values to hexadecimal.
scheme: Easier or quicker to read, write or understand
Easier or quicker to identify errors or debug
Takes up less screen or display space

steps.label: Where Hexadecimal Is Used
steps.content:
Where Hexadecimal Is Used

Think → Pair → ShareEvery use below is a long binary value that a person has to read or type. Predict: which of these have you seen before?Show the worked answer

Colour codes in web pages, MAC addresses on a network, and error codes on a screen are the ones most people have seen.

  • HTML colour codes: #FF8000 (red, green, blue).
  • MAC addresses: 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E (48 bits).
  • Error codes: 404, 12B.
  • Memory addresses and memory dumps.
  • Assembly language (low-level programming).
  • IP addresses (IPv6) and URLs.
A MAC address in binary
0000 0000 0001 1010 0010 1011 0011 1100 0100 1101 0101 1110
The same MAC address in hexadecimal
00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E

steps.label: How a Colour Code Works
steps.content:
How a Colour Code Works

Think → Pair → ShareA colour code has 3 pairs of digits: red, green and blue. Predict: why is the largest pair FF, and what is FF in denary?Show the worked answer

Each pair is 2 digits, so 8 bits. The largest 8-bit value is 1111 1111, which is FF, which is 255.

  • #RRGGBB: the first pair is red, then green, then blue.
  • Each pair is 8 bits: 00 (none) to FF (255, full).
  • #FF0000 is full red. #000000 is black. #FFFFFF is white.
  • Hexadecimal is used because 6 digits are easier to read and type than 24 bits.
#FF0000
#000000
#FFFFFF
#FF8000
